I am 63 years old and have farmed these fields in Quzhou for 48 years. I never went to school, but the land has been my teacher. With 11 mouths to feed and some of my children working off-farm, I must be careful with my labor and my 8 mu of land. The wheat-maize rotation is my backbone — it feeds the family and the livestock — but cotton brings in cash, and mungbean is good for the soil and adds variety to our meals.

This year, I will put **5.5 mu into the wheat-maize double crop**. Wheat is sown in October after rotary tillage. I will use an improved variety like the ones my neighbors have had success with. I know wheat is hungry for nitrogen, so I will apply compound fertilizer as a basal dose and topdress with urea at jointing. I will irrigate three times from my well — overwinter, at jointing, and at flowering — because dry springs are common here. I also spray pesticides four times to control aphids and fungus. I expect about 1,000 jin per mu.

When the wheat comes off in early June, I will immediately sow **hybrid maize** on the same 5.5 mu using **no-tillage**. There is no time to waste between harvests, and the stubble helps keep moisture in the ground. Maize needs less nitrogen than wheat because some fertility remains, but I will give it compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress urea later. Two irrigations will be enough — one when it is knee-high and one at filling stage. Three pesticide sprays should handle the borers and weeds. I expect around 1,100 jin per mu.

I will keep **2 mu for cotton**. I am getting older, and cotton is heavy work with all the pruning and spraying, so I cannot manage more than that. I will rotary-till in spring and plant a hybrid variety. Cotton needs plenty of potassium and phosphorus for the bolls, so I will put down a good dose of compound fertilizer. I will irrigate twice and spray pesticides many times — probably 14 times — because the bollworms and aphids never rest in Quzhou. I hope for about 550 jin of seed cotton per mu.

On the edges of the cotton field and a small corner plot, I will grow **half a mu of mungbean**. It fixes nitrogen and does not need much attention. I will use the **traditional seeds** I saved from last year, give them some compound fertilizer, irrigate twice if the weather turns dry, and spray a few times for insects. I expect about 90 jin per mu. 

This plan balances food security, cash income, and the limited labor I have with my family working away.
